kicker: Life insurance · new sales vs value of new business, Q2 FY27
title: Life insurers' profit on new policies outgrew sales
dek: At all five, VNB (the profit value of new policies) grew faster than APE (new sales) as mix tilted to protection cover. HDFC Life rose 4.23% on 12 Nov; calls say the GST exemption lifted cover sales but cost insurers tax credits.

read: Life insurers are earning more on each policy rather than selling many more of them, so H2 depends on sales picking up as protection growth laps the post-GST surge.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 earnings calls; HDFC Life share move: 5paisa, 12 Nov 2026

companies.name: ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Ltd

notes: VNB (value of new business) is the present value of future profits on policies sold in the period; APE (annualised premium equivalent) is a standard measure of new sales, and VNB margin is VNB divided by APE. Growth rates are as stated on each Q2 FY27 call for H1 FY27 year on year: individual APE for HDFC Life, SBI Life and Axis Max Life (Max Financial), total APE for LIC, and for Bajaj Life (Bajaj Finserv) Q2 retail weighted received premium and Q2 VNB; HDFC Life's call summary gives individual APE growth of 9% in its highlights and guidance but 11% in its overview, and either way VNB (+12%) grew faster. A dumbbell of margins was not possible because only four insurers gave a year-ago margin (HDFC Life 24.5%→24.7%, LIC 17.6%→22.3%, Axis Max Life 23.3%→25.4%, Bajaj Life 17.1%→21.6% for Q2); ICICI Prudential Life grew VNB 22.3% with protection APE up 39.5% but gave no total APE growth, so it is not charted. GST: individual life policies were exempted from GST in September 2025, which made cover cheaper for buyers (Axis Max Life said 80–85% of its post-exemption protection buyers were new customers, and HDFC Life is lapping 57% protection growth in H2 FY26), but insurers can no longer claim input tax credit on commissions and costs; SBI Life booked a one-off H1 GST impact of ₹530 crore, and Axis Max Life expects commission and GST adjustments to cut costs. News hook: HDFC Life shares rose 4.23% to ₹597.80 on 12 Nov 2026 (5paisa). Caveats: margins also moved with interest-rate (yield-curve) assumptions, which SBI Life said added about 70 bps, and IRDAI's draft caps on distribution commissions could change margins again.
